overview: IMAP manages mail stored on the server. Clients select mailboxes, fetch selected content and synchronize flags, allowing multiple devices to work with the same mailbox state.
outro: The client selected INBOX and fetched content by UID while leaving the message on the server. IDLE then allowed the server to announce a mailbox change. This separation of server storage, content retrieval and state updates supports synchronized clients.
steps: The client connects to port 993 and establishes TLS before speaking IMAP. Protection applies to credentials, mailbox metadata and content. The server then sends its protocol greeting.
A tagged command authenticates the user inside TLS. The server repeats that tag in its completion response. Tags let a client associate responses with commands even when unsolicited updates arrive.
SELECT opens INBOX for message operations. The server reports message count, flags and UID validity information. Stable UIDs are more useful for synchronization than sequence numbers that may shift.

The client fetches a message or a selected part of it. BODY.PEEK avoids setting the Seen flag merely by retrieving the data. The message remains on the server unless an explicit removal workflow is used.
The client enters IDLE to receive mailbox changes without repeated polling. A server update can announce a new message. DONE ends IDLE so the client can issue further commands.
